meaning_by_symbol.C: cloth; drape the cloth over the entire device at once, covering all faces simultaneously when used as a tool instruction
meaning_by_symbol.S: stone; place the stone beside the named face, not on top; when used with each face, move the stone to each face one at a time
meaning_by_symbol.B: bell; chime the bell near the named location, not touching the device
meaning_by_symbol.F: fan; wave air at the named faces simultaneously, not sequentially
meaning_by_symbol.P: board; rest the board flat against the named face
meaning_by_symbol.R: rotate the device slowly and steadily
meaning_by_symbol.opp: the face directly opposite the named face
meaning_by_symbol.ea: each; apply in turn to each item in the set
meaning_by_symbol.adj: adjacent to or bordering the named face; for cloth on adjacent edges, the two edges that border the named face
meaning_by_symbol.trace: after the stone step, run a fingertip along each edge of the named face; for face tracing, trace only the four edges of that named face, not all twelve edges of the device
meaning_by_symbol.CornerProc: for each corner of the named face, chime the bell, then place the stone on both edges meeting at that corner, hold for the specified duration, gentle
meaning_by_symbol.RotateProc: rotate slowly for the specified duration while holding a tone at the named face and its opposite face simultaneously, then bell once at each corner
meaning_by_symbol.Scors: place the stone near each of the four corners of the named face, one corner at a time, for the specified duration per corner at the given intensity; the stone should be near the corner, not touching it
meaning_by_symbol.Bctr: chime the bell near the center of a face

reply.rationale: No multi-entry compositional paradigm is securely supported. Although some symbols contain apparent substrings also listed independently (e.g. Bctr vs B + ctr, Scors vs S + cors, CornerProc/RotateProc vs *Proc), the required paradigm evidence is missing. There is no stable substitution frame with contrasting fillers whose meaning contributions remain consistent across multiple whole codes. In particular: (1) 'Proc' does not contribute a predictable shared meaning across CornerProc and RotateProc; these are best treated as opaque procedure names. (2) 'ors' and 'tr' do not form validated suffix classes, because the residues do not participate in a coherent shared construction with predictable whole meanings. Scors adds duration/intensity/per-corner procedural content not recoverable from S + cors. (3) cor/cors are semantically related, but there is no productive frame showing a number-like alternation inside larger codes. Since false morphology is worse than a flat lexicon, all symbols are treated as lexical.
